# Morse — The signal studio: full product notes

Morse Studio is a static client-side web application. The website provides an overview, text-to-Morse encoder, Morse-to-text decoder, alphabet/prosign reference, practice quiz, About page and Cipher Lab.

## Morse translation
International Morse letters A-Z, digits 0-9, punctuation and common prosigns are supported. A slash separates words. An app-specific Arabic/Urdu extension table is included; it is a convenience mapping and must not be treated as a single globally standardized encoding. Audio timing exposes WPM and Farnsworth spacing and tone frequency. Light and vibration output are best-effort device capabilities. Tap-key controls accept dots, dashes, letter gaps and word gaps.

## Cipher Lab: Codebook
A personal codebook maps words to emoji sequences. Templates can be customized, unknown words use a character-level fallback alphabet, and JSON import/export is available. This mode is reversible obfuscation and does not provide confidentiality against someone who can inspect the mapping or infer it.

## Cipher Lab: Secure
The application uses Web Crypto AES-256-GCM. A key is derived from the user's passphrase using PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 with 600,000 iterations. Each encryption generates a cryptographically random 16-byte salt and 12-byte GCM nonce. The JSON envelope is represented as emoji pairs (hexadecimal nibbles encoded with emoji). Decryption authenticates the message; a wrong passphrase or modified ciphertext fails authentication. The passphrase is not stored. Do not reuse weak passwords. Secure URL fragments are bearer secrets and should be shared privately.

## Data handling
No server receives plaintext, passphrases, codebooks or ciphertext during normal operation. The app may persist theme, encrypted saved codebook and a short local history in browser storage. A panic wipe clears the app's local storage and caches on the current browser origin.

## Accessibility and offline
Semantic controls, visible focus styles, labels and reduced-motion CSS are included. A service worker caches the application shell for offline use after first visit. Browser/device support varies for vibration, audio and screen flashing.

## Contact / brand
Built by CloudExify. CloudExify Technologies (Private) Limited, Islamabad. https://cloudexify.site


## Update 2: ECDH contacts
The Contacts screen supports P-256 ECDH public-key exchange. Each contact has a local ECDH key pair; private PKCS#8 material and contact records are stored inside an AES-GCM encrypted vault. The vault key is derived from a local PIN with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 (310,000 iterations), a random salt and nonce. Peers derive an AES-256-GCM key using ECDH and HKDF-SHA-256. A safety fingerprint consists of four emoji and a six-digit code; users must compare it over a separate trusted channel. Rotating a contact key requires the peer to import the new public key and verify the new fingerprint. Revocation removes local key material but cannot revoke copies held by the peer.

## Expiring and view-once contact messages
ECDH contact messages carry an authenticated expiry timestamp and a view-once preference inside the encrypted payload. The decoder rejects expired messages. Fixed-size padding rounds plaintext payloads into buckets, which hides exact length but reveals the selected bucket. View-once clears the local display after a short delay; it cannot prevent screenshots, memory inspection or saving the plaintext.

## PWA sharing and additional pages
The PWA manifest declares a POST share target at /share. The service worker intercepts the form locally, stores the draft in Cache Storage and redirects to /share without putting message content in the URL or sending it to the application server. Contacts, Privacy, How it works and Share routes are added to the app shell and sitemap. The same-origin frame policy permits same-origin iframe embedding; this does not itself constitute a finished embeddable widget SDK.

## Current scope notes
The ECDH contact flow and the associated crypto core are implemented as a separate feature from the legacy passphrase Secure mode. Existing Update 1 codebooks, ciphertext and Secret Room links retain their old format. See docs/MIGRATION-UPDATE-2.md and docs/THREAT-MODEL.md. Camera decoding, microphone decoding, image steganography, decoy messages, zero-width/word-list disguise, full four-language UI translation, Argon2id WASM, Diceware, Chrome extension, npm package publishing and a finished iframe widget are not represented as completed features in this build.
